events.region: Mora, NM; San Miguel, NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Hermits Peak Calf Canyon burn scar in...
Southwestern Mora County in northeastern New Mexico...
Northwestern San Miguel County in northeastern New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 144 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Hermits Peak Calf Canyon Burn Scar. Up to 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is likely
ongoing with a significant flood crest heading down area streams.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Beaver Creek,
Sapello River, Manuelitas Creek, Rito San Jose, and Rito Cebolla. The
debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Hermits Peak Calf Canyon
Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Hermits Peak Calf Canyon Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tierra Monte, Sapello, El Porvenir, Ledoux, Montezuma, Morphy Lake
State Park, Manuelitas, South Carmen and Gallinas.

This includes State Road 518 between Mile Markers 10 and 14...and
between Mile Markers 17 and 20.

This also includes Sebastian Canyon.
